title: GPU OOM cascade combined with KV-index drift: stability guardian and runtime mitigation
creator: Maya Chen
description: Multiple customers across Hosted, Dedicated and Private fleets reported recurrent GPU OOM spikes over the last three weeks. These events coincide with high prefix-sharing workloads and long-lived sessions; post-incident traces show KV index divergence (stale tombstones and fragmented slot maps) followed by aggressive allocator behaviour that precipitates cascade OOMs. This ticket tracks investigation, interim mitigations (hotpatch), and the production runtime fix to stabilize eviction/allocations and ensure KV-index consistency under heavy churn.
reproduction_steps: 1) Deploy a long-running session workload with frequent small requests that reuse prefixes (simulate chatbots with long context and many short messages)
2) Configure prefix caching enabled and set request concurrency to 180% of typical per-GPU throughput to force evictions
3) Run synthetic mixed-length sequences (mean length 120 tokens, 20% tail >512 tokens) for 2 hours
4) Observe allocator fragmentation metrics (slab_utilization, free_run_count) and KV-index tombstone backlog via /internal/debug endpoints
5) Confirm trigger: progressive growth of tombstone count + failed index reconciliations → sudden slab exhaustion → GPU OOMs followed by session failovers
investigation_findings: Hotpath: under sustained small-request patterns the KV index accumulates tombstones faster than the compactor can sweep; combined with token-length spikes this causes large transient allocations in the tensor arena
Allocator behavior: free fragments exist but are partitioned across arenas; cross-arena coalescing is not aggressive enough, leaving unusable fragments
KV-layer: index resyncs occasionally race with evict operations, producing short-lived inconsistencies that cause double-evict attempts and temporary handle leaks

Observed across environments: Hosted saw fastest saturation due to multi-tenant density; Dedicated customers with large pools experienced slower drift but same endpoint failure; Private installs reported manifests only when older runtime (1.22) lacked tombstone heuristics
Customer escalations: 3 enterprise P1 tickets opened in last 10 days; two customers suffered >5% request failures during business hours
root_cause: A combination of KV-index tombstone accumulation and allocator fragmentation under high-churn small-request workloads. Race windows between index reconciliation and eviction permit transient handle leakage; fragmentation prevents timely reuse of freed GPU memory leading to cascade OOMs when a large allocation is requested.
fix_summary: Deliver a multi-part runtime patch: (A) introduce an eviction-throttle gate to reduce concurrent evict+resync work and eliminate handle double-free races; (B) add a compact-on-threshold compaction heuristic that triggers inter-arena coalescing earlier; (C) place a checksum guard on index resyncs to reject conflicting deltas and queue them for serial reconciliation; (D) ship a targeted allocator fallback that returns larger contiguous spans for tail requests when fragmentation above threshold is detected.
work_items: Implement eviction-throttle gate and unit tests (Lukas)
Add inter-arena coalescer + smoke tests for fragmentation scenarios (engine team)
Index checksum + serial reconciliation queue and e2e tests (data-integrity)
Hotpatch for hosted fleet: deploy eviction-throttle only to reduce blast radius and monitor (operational runbook)
Backport compatible patch for runtime-1.22 for private deployments (engineering support)
Update canary harness: add churny small-request scenario and long-tail token spikes
rollout_plan: 1) Merge patch to runtime-main behind feature flag 'evict_gate'
2) Deploy to staging clusters and run 72h synthetic churn test (must show <1 OOM/hour across cluster)
3) Canary rollout to 2% of hosted traffic with aggressive telemetry (oom_count, tombstone_rate, allocator_frag_score)
4) Observe for 48h; if metrics stable, expand to 20% and run customer smoke tests with two impacted customers (coordinate with SEs)
5) Gradual ramp to 100% for hosted; schedule dedicated and private upgrades during low-impact maintenance windows and offer backports for Private customers still on 1.22
rollback_plan: Feature-flagged rollback: flip 'evict_gate' to off and revert allocator fallback. If rollback doesn't stabilize, revert to previous runtime build via standard fleet rollback (documented in runbook). Notify affected customers and open incident bridge for immediate follow-up.
monitoring_queries: handle_leak_alert: increase in kv_handle_open_count without corresponding close over 10m
acceptance_criteria: No P1 customer escalations attributable to same root cause for 14 days post-full-rollout
OOM rate across hosted clusters reduced by >= 90% for the reproduced churn workload
KV-index checksum mismatches reduced to 0 in canary for 72h
Allocator fragmentation 95th percentile score improved by at least 40% under synthetic test
Backport validated on one private customer image and documented upgrade steps
postmortem_actions: Add a scheduled tombstone-compaction job for long-lived sessions with configurable cadence
Expose a new console metric 'kv.tombstones.pending' and alert on >1000 per-host
Create best-practice doc for customers: recommended prefix-cache TTLs and session churn knobs
Automate a periodic inter-arena coalescing during low-util windows
Ship integration tests in CI that simulate small-request churn and confirm no OOMs
